text: 3 – ICE-31® Parametric Testing 7.3.1 Flue Gas Temperature The flue gas flow rate was held constant. The flue gas temperature was varied to determine the change in SRD when capture efficiency was held constant. All system parameters were held constant except solvent flow rate and stripper temperature (and thus steam); these two parameters were varied as needed to maintain capture efficiency at nominally 95%. 7.3.2 Baseline The flue gas flow rate and temperature were held constant. Solvent flow rate and cold-rich bypass ratio varied. Stripper pressure, and stripper steam flow were held constant. The capture efficiency and SRD varied with changing solvent flow rate. The stripper sump temperature varied when steam flow was held constant while the solvent flow rate changed. The objective was to find the maximum capture efficiency. 7.3.3 Steam Turndown The flue gas flow rate and temperature were held constant. The solvent flow rate was varied to achieve the desired capture efficiency. Cold-rich bypass flow was held relatively constant. Stripper pressure was held constant. Stripper steam flow was allowed to vary, as was the sump temperature (slightly). The objective was to determine the SRD as solvent flow rate was changed to achieve specified capture efficiencies. 7.3.4 Flue Gas Turndown ION operated the system with varying flue gas flow rates. Flue gas temperature was held constant, as was solvent flow rate, and stripper pressure. Stripper sump temperature varied slightly, as did the cold-rich bypass. The capture efficiency and SRD varied as dependent variables. The objective was to evaluate turndown performance with ICE-31®. In theory, maintaining solvent flow rate and steam flow constant while reducing flue gas flow rate should result in a measurable increase in capture efficiency and SRD. ION Clean Energy 19 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT 7.3.5 High Pressure Baseline The stripper was operated at high pressure. Higher stripper pressure (and resulting increase in temperature) allowed for more efficient and selective recovery of CO in the stripper sump. Stripper 2 pressure was still constant. The flue gas flow rate and temperature were held constant. Solvent flow rate varied. Cold-rich bypass ratio and stripper steam flow were held constant. The capture efficiency and SRD varied with changing solvent flow rate. The stripper sump temperature varied when steam flow was held constant while the solvent flow rate changed. 7.3.6 High Pressure Steam Turndown The stripper was operated at high pressure. Stripper pressure was constant. The flue gas flow rate and temperature were held constant. The solvent flow rate was varied to achieve the desired capture efficiency. Cold-rich bypass flow was held relatively constant. Stripper steam flow was allowed to vary to maintain constant sump temperature. The objective was to determine the SRD as solvent flow rate was changed to achieve specified capture efficiencies. 7.3.7 High Pressure Flue Gas Turndown The stripper was operated at high pressure. Stripper pressure was constant. ION operated the system with varying flue gas flow rates. Flue gas temperature was held constant, as was the solvent flow rate and cold-rich bypass ratio. Stripper sump temperature varied slightly. The capture efficiency and SRD varied as dependent variables.
